requirement: Mandatory core; optional packs; authenticated database-per-tenant routing across all API/worker/read/admin/maintenance paths. Shared instance and API service allowed. No default fallback.
current_evidence: api/app.py lifespan creates Settings() and process-local app.state stores, bundle, retrieval and artifact retriever
api/dependencies.py resolves request.app.state (already avoids global settings singleton)
worker/__main__.py run_worker creates Settings(); subscriptions and stores share its configured database
ontology/runtime.py caches immutable ActiveBundle by pack settings and reconstructs registry snapshots
ontology/versioning.py persists OntologyState:active graph node per database, not tenant ownership or atomic admission/version fence
candidate: Immutable server-side tenant catalog maps tenant identity to unique authorized database resource, exact pack bundle and API/admin credential identity. Reject duplicated database bindings and ambiguous credentials. Never authorize from payload/agent_id/database/header alone.

Prefer reusing existing app.state boundary: configure a child FastAPI application/runtime per tenant within one authenticated dispatcher. create_app/lifespan accept explicit settings instead of mutating process environment. Dispatcher resolves credential to tenant before selecting child app; dependency/store/retrieval caches remain child-local. This is a candidate, compare against request-scoped runtime dependency injection.

Webhooks need explicit server-resolved source/tenant binding plus tenant-specific verified signature; a tenant path selects candidates but is not authentication. No unsigned webhook can append, and shared signing secrets must not silently authorize multiple tenants.

Worker and admin CLI use the same catalog plus explicit authorized tenant target and exact interpretation revision. Worker processes may be pinned per tenant; shared service does not require shared worker state. Every consumer group/checkpoint/retention operation uses that database and runtime, no default.

Persist an explicit tenant/database/bundle binding and verify it before serving or processing. Determine minimal atomic fencing of accepted event interpretation and worker writes during activation; startup checks alone cannot prove no stale acceptance. Reuse OntologyState where safe; add dedicated state only when required, and distinguish transport envelope from pack payload.

Historical visibility follows active scoped reads; disable/re-enable/catch-up and replay retain pinned original contracts. Explicitly authorized same-tenant rebuild targets must not permit another tenant database or switch the ledger by accident.
No new orchestration service, per-combination branches, Redis/Neo4j runner or automatic adapter framework.
review_dimensions: Choose the smallest complete routing architecture grounded in current factories/dependencies; enumerate every route/background/CLI cache bypass.
Authentication and admin/webhook authorization, catalog validation and unique bindings, credential rotation and failure isolation.
Pack/version pinning, durable admission/worker fences, stale runtimes and recovery, historical reads and activation policy.
Resource lifecycle and bounded pools/cache reuse; preserve specialized processing and disabled capability gates.
Adversarial two-database colliding-ID acceptance for events/sessions/users/entities/artifacts/cursors/evaluation/replay/deletion/retention; real Engram Spanner assertions and forbidden effects.
Concrete implementation slices/dependencies and what must be settled now versus safe explicit later limits; identify any true product decision rather than guessing.
deliverable: Verdict plus prioritized gaps with source evidence, recommended concrete minimal contract and slice sequence, exact required acceptance. Read-only source review; write review report only. No tests/cloud/runtime changes.
